extracted.intended_audience: general readers and news consumers interested in technology, media ethics, and AI
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluative and procedural standards for AI-generated news push notifications and summaries — covering accuracy, labeling, opt-in consent, and safety/rollback practices. Focused on how news organizations, platform developers, and regulators should treat AI‑produced news alerts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy / Reliability of summaries
rubrics_metrics.description: AI summaries must accurately reflect original reporting and must not invent or misstate facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article documents multiple failures where Apple Intelligence produced 'misleading or altogether false summaries' (e.g., falsely stating Luigi Mangione 'had shot himself', and summarizing three NYT articles as if Netanyahu had been arrested). BBC: 'the accuracy of our news is essential in maintaining trust.' Anti-patterns: fabrications/hallucinations that contradict original content; scoring note: a summary that changes factual claims is unacceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency / explicit labeling as AI-produced
rubrics_metrics.description: Notifications and summaries produced by AI should explicitly emphasize that the information has been produced by AI and may be inaccurate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apple said it would make summaries 'more explicitly emphasize that the information has been produced by AI' when re-enabled. This helps users recognize output may be unreliable. Guidance from the article: label AI output clearly to avoid confusing it with editorial or reporter-written headlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opt-in consent for AI summaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Users must be able to opt into AI-generated news summaries rather than having them forced on all users.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article notes the Apple Intelligence summaries 'users must opt into.' Procedural requirement: features that can alter how news is presented should require user opt-in to avoid unwitting exposure to AI‑generated content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safety-first deployment / disable until fixed
rubrics_metrics.description: Platforms should disable or roll back AI news features if they repeatedly produce incorrect or harmful output and only re-enable after fixes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apple deployed a beta update that disabled the AI feature for news and entertainment headlines while it 'works to improve the AI feature' and plans to re-enable later. Press groups called for removal. Anti-pattern: continuing to push erroneous summaries to users during known failure modes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not conflate or misattribute across stories
rubrics_metrics.description: AI should not merge multiple articles into a single notification in ways that create false composite claims or misattribute events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example from the article: 'three New York Times articles were also summarized in a single push notification, falsely stating that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu had been arrested.' This illustrates the risk of conflation; guidance is to preserve source boundaries and avoid compressing separate reports into one misleading alert.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect public right to reliable information / maintain trust
rubrics_metrics.description: News platforms and developers must prioritize the public's right to reliable information and avoid placing the public in a position of 'second-guessing' news accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporters Without Borders called the summaries 'a danger to the public's right to reliable information on current affairs,' and the National Union of Journalists emphasized 'the public must not be placed in a position of second-guessing the accuracy of news they receive.' Scoring: practices that undermine public trust are unacceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize limits of large-language models / require verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Because LLMs are trained to produce 'plausible sounding' answers without inherent 'knowledge of truth,' outputs should be subject to verification and human oversight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article cites Suresh Venkatasubramanian: LLMs produce 'plausible sounding' answers whether accurate or made up; Cornell/University of Washington/Waterloo study: top models still 'can't be fully trusted.' Guidance: implement human review, fact-checking, or conservative presentation (e.g., not stating AI summaries as definitive facts).
